# Upcoming Webinars {.mt-0}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

source("../R/render-events.R")

cat(render_events("../data/events.yaml", type = "webinars"))
```

**Abstract**: Spatial computational models, such as agent-based models (ABMs),
provide powerful in silico tools for studying tumor dynamics. However, their
parameterization remains challenging, while imaging data are still underused for
directly informing model development. We develop ABMs to investigate regulatory
mechanisms in the tumor microenvironment across biological scales. We also
develop computational pipelines to analyze and optimize these models, combining
imaging data with feature-extraction approaches like convolutional encoders. Our
goal is to establish flexible frameworks for ABM development, training, and
analysis, enabling spatial models to more effectively incorporate image-derived
information and ultimately support the study of oncogenic interactions and drug
responses.
